Allah's Right Hand stays full despite all He has spent since creating the heavens and earth; His Throne is over the water and He raises and lowers people.
Zainab boasted Allah married her to the Prophet from above seven heavens; the verse on what the Prophet hid concerned her and Zaid, and the Hijab verse concerned her.
When Allah finished His creation, He wrote over His Throne: 'My Mercy preceded My Anger'.
Allah will admit to Paradise whoever believes, prays and fasts Ramadan; it has a hundred degrees for those in jihad, and Firdaus, its highest, lies beneath the Beneficent's Throne.
The Prophet said the sun asks permission to prostrate, and one day will be told to return and rise in the west; he recited the verse on its course.
Sent by Abu Bakr to collect the Quran, Zaid bin Thabit found the last verses of Surat at-Tauba with Abu Khuzaima Al-Ansari alone.
In distress the Prophet said there is no god but Allah, the Knowing and Forbearing, Lord of the Mighty Throne, Lord of the heavens and earth.
When people fall unconscious on Resurrection, the Prophet, the first to be raised, will see Moses holding a pillar of the Throne.
Angels of the night and day meet at the Asr and Fajr prayers; those ascending tell Allah, who knows best, that they left His slaves praying and found them praying.
Allah takes charity of a date's value from honest earnings in His Right Hand and grows it like a foal into a mountain, for only good ascends to Him.
In distress the Prophet declared none worthy of worship but Allah, the Majestic and Forbearing, Lord of the Tremendous Throne and of the heavens.
A man rebuked the Prophet's gold gifts to Najd chiefs; the Prophet foretold the man's offspring would include Quran reciters who leave Islam like an arrow and kill Muslims.
Asked about the verse on the sun running its fixed course, the Prophet said its fixed course is beneath Allah's Throne.
Looking at the full moon, the Prophet told those with him they will see their Lord as clearly, so they should not miss the prayers before sunrise and sunset.
Believers will see their Lord like the full moon; each people follows what it worshipped, a bridge spans Hell, believers intercede, and the last man out of Hell enters Paradise.
Believers on Resurrection go from Adam to Jesus, then to Muhammad, who intercedes three times and takes people out of Hell; this is the Station of Praise promised him.
The Prophet gathered the Ansar in a tent and told them to be patient until they meet Allah and His Messenger, who will be at the Kauthar.
In his night prayer the Prophet praised Allah as Keeper and Light of the heavens and earth, affirmed that His word, Paradise and Hell are true, and asked forgiveness.
Everyone's Lord will speak to him with no interpreter or screen, and in the Paradise of Eden only the Cover of Majesty over His Face keeps people from seeing Him.
Whoever takes a Muslim's property by false oath will meet Allah angry; Allah will neither speak to nor look at false swearers over sales, nor withholders of surplus water.
On the Day of Nahr the Prophet said four of the twelve months are sacred, and that lives, property and honour are as sacred as that day, town and month.
Weeping over a dying grandson, the Prophet said Allah is merciful to the merciful; Paradise is His Mercy, Hell His Punishment; some scorched in Hell enter Paradise by His Mercy.
A Jewish rabbi said Allah will put the heavens, earth and all creation each on a finger and say 'I am the King'; the Prophet smiled and recited a verse.
The Prophet rose in the last third of the night, looked at the sky reciting the verse on the creation of the heavens and earth, and prayed eleven rak'at.
When Allah created the creation, He wrote with Him on His Throne: 'My Mercy has preceded My Anger'.
In the womb an angel writes each person's livelihood, death, deeds and whether wretched or blessed, and what is written decides his final deeds, leading to Paradise or Hell.
The Prophet asked Gabriel why he did not visit more often, and the verse came down that the angels descend only by the command of his Lord.
Jews in Medina asked the Prophet about the spirit, and he answered with the revealed verse that its knowledge is with his Lord and mankind has little knowledge.
Allah guarantees Paradise, or return with reward or booty, to one going out solely for jihad in His Cause; only fighting so Allah's Word is superior is in His Cause.
A group of the Prophet's followers will remain victorious and keep to Allah's commands, unharmed by those who oppose them, until Allah's Order, the Hour, comes.
The Prophet told Musailama he would not give him a palm stalk; he cannot escape what Allah ordained for him, and if he turned from Islam Allah would ruin him.
Jews asked the Prophet about the spirit; after a pause in which he was being inspired, he answered with the verse that its knowledge is with his Lord.
Allah guarantees one who goes out solely for jihad in His Cause, believing His Word, either Paradise or a return home with reward or booty.
When asking Allah, be firm and do not say 'if You wish', for no one can compel Him.
Asked at night whether he and Fatima would pray, Ali said their souls are in Allah's Hand; the Prophet left striking his thighs, saying man is most quarrelsome.
A believer is like a fresh plant bent by the wind that straightens again after calamities, and a disbeliever like a stiff pine that stands until Allah cuts it down.
The Muslims' time beside earlier nations is like Asr to sunset, yet they earn double the people of the Torah and Gospel, as Allah grants His favour as He wishes.

The pledge to the Prophet bars associating partners with Allah, stealing, illegal intercourse, killing offspring, slander and disobedience; punishment in this world expiates, and screened sins rest with Allah.
Had Solomon said 'If Allah wills', each wife would have borne a horseman for Allah's Cause; the Prophet told a sick bedouin his fever purifies, if Allah wills.
When the people overslept the morning prayer, the Prophet said Allah took their souls and returned them when He willed, and he prayed after the sun had risen.
